Maintain District standards of excellent customer service and professional behavior in various and sometimes challenging situations.
Access and monitor District email daily to receive important updates from school and District administration.
Participate in staff development and in-service training programs as assigned.
Complete daily acquisition skills, maintenance, and mastered skills as directed by BCBA

Collect, record, and summarize data on observable student behavior; document interventions, report progress on goals, and record session notes; collect data for behavior assessments and any additional programming as directed by a credentialed teacher, supervisor or BCBA.
Assist with staff training and implementation of behavior plans, behavior-related accommodations and IEP goals, data collection procedures, and preparation of related materials
Provide recommendations and modeling of Tier 1 and Tier 2 behavioral strategies to classroom teachers/staff, school sites and student support teams.
Work with multiple students of varying ages and abilities across a variety of educational settings at multiple sites throughout the school year, as directed by immediate supervisor.
Exercise supervision of students; observes, monitors, and redirects behavior of students within approved procedures.
Model effective instructional and behavioral support strategies for Instructional Assistants; provide in-the moment coaching and peer mentorship.
Support students during classroom activities, transitions, field trips, and playground; assist students in developing appropriate behavioral, social, and functional skills.
Assist students with physical, medical, and/or personal hygiene needs, including but not limited to: monitoring of medical conditions, lifting, dressing, feeding, and toileting/diapering
Must observe confidentiality and be discrete in responding to student behaviors.
Immediately report any incidents or behavior intervention challenges to RBT supervisor

Attend regular department meetings with RBT supervisors and/or other RBTs, and engage in the planning, material preparation, and presentation of professional development opportunities for district staff.
Abide by the ethical guidelines outlined by the Behavior Analyst Certification Board.
May be required to maintain RBT certification, including annual renewal and registration or similar District directed training.
May be assigned out of class work as prescribed by Merit Rules and Regulations.
